scope: Current product architecture. Legacy source remains captured by the AppSDK source module until separately removed.

modules.note: Owns logical Endpoint identity, descriptor, capability/resource attachment and endpoint lifecycle; E1 registry is implemented. Does not own routes, transport or Work ledger
Fixed CLI execution and local browser handles; no provider resource ledger or daemon ownership

User-facing agentteams init/start/status/work/stop facade; init delegates v3 bootstrap to initializeLocalConfig and lifecycle delegates to the compiled runtime local launcher. It owns no TLS, child projection, capability implementation or network truth. Candidate evidence: c3c2e0e; U2 continuation: docs/evidence/776fcad-u2-config-impl-20261003/. The ACP `--serve <opencode|dsh> --ip --port` entry is delivered here: cli/agentteams.mjs parses the flags and dispatches to runtime/acp-serve.ts, which starts one daemon plus one engine child with the OpenCode or DSH adapter selected by runtime/acp-serve.ts engineAdapterFor. No compile-only placeholder exists. D04 adds the `agentteams registry start|status|stop --config <file> [--generation <n>]` verbs; they delegate lifecycle truth to runtime/registry-process.ts and start no other daemon.

Owns the source-level local Work Unix socket seam only: typed decode/encode, listener admission, peer drain and own-socket cleanup, plus the single failed or unconfirmed Work receipt projection from a typed frame. It is not the CLI facade, receiver dispatch, config internal owner, or installed runtime.
Owns the single staged package producer, base asset/CLI smoke, installed lifecycle restart smoke, and lifecycle receipt binding. Final SDK runner/graph inclusion remains a D3/U4 input dependency.

Owns link configuration, transport, health and route execution. D04 adds `network/registration-client.ts` as the client transport/health owner for registry registration: it connects the config-selected discovery endpoint over wss, registers, renews the presence lease with a heartbeat, reconnects with bounded backoff on the same endpoint and keeps the original error instead of switching servers. It imports no `config/**`; the config-selected discovery plan and the AgentDeclaration stay in runtime. Gate: teams-acp-d04-registry.

Canonical owner of the Console observation wire contract. BB09 round 12 adds the optional capabilityDetails declaration summary to the shared runtime|directory Agent row fields, its closed parser validation (existing string and capacity/unit checks; illegal shapes rejected, never stripped) and the single declaration-to-summary helper reused by the runtime and Console-hub producers. D00 adds the public ACP envelope and single fault carrier (acp.ts), the type-only engine adapter port (engine.ts), the Teams negotiation frames and the connection-state/history DTOs (teams-connection.ts, teams-state.ts); declarations and parsers only, with transport, negotiation and history reads pending D01/D05/D06.

Owns Session, RPC/callback correlation, execution admission and execution history semantics. D01 (merged 7d0bca4, fixed 75a6cf4) implements `agent-host/acp-host.ts` and the append-only write port `agent-host/acp-history.ts`: per-channel id correlation, explicit Session ownership, D00 policy before any engine write, append-before-effect with separate history-fault reporting, cancel.requested versus the prompt's terminal result, RESULT_UNKNOWN on engine exit or channel close, and bounded delivery/notification records. Status is partial, not implemented: the D02 OpenCode engine adapter and the `--serve opencode` entry exist, but the network channel (D05) and the DSH serve wiring do not (the D03 DSH adapter exists at source level), so the host has no installed/live product evidence; its real-engine exercise is the committed D02 CLI black box and the D03 evidence driver, not an installed entry.

Owner of the engine-independent stdio ACP transport between an engine child and agent-host. D01 (merged 7d0bca4, fixed 75a6cf4) implements `acp-adapter/stdio.ts` as the newline-delimited JSON `AcpDuplex` over the frozen `control-protocol/engine.ts` port, with CRLF tolerance, a maxFrameBytes bound, typed transport faults and clean-EOF settlement; `acp-adapter/test-peer.mjs` is a labeled test peer, not an engine. The directory exists now. Status is partial, not implemented: the D03 DSH adapter and the D02 OpenCode adapter each compile a real `EngineLaunchSpec` (see the dsh-adapter and opencode-adapter modules), and runtime/acp-serve.ts dispatches both engine kinds over this one transport; installed-copy engine inference is still not proven here. Gate: teams-acp-d01-host.

Owner of the DSH engine adapter: it derives the real DSH native profile patch from the accepted Teams config, compiles the single `EngineLaunchSpec` for the `dsh` kind, and reads the real `initialize`/`session/new` results back as an effectiveness proof. D03 (frozen candidate 60bf76b, merged here) implements `dsh-adapter/index.ts` and `dsh-adapter/native-config.ts` with 28 focused specs, and `dsh-adapter/real-engine-evidence.mjs` is committed evidence tooling that drove the real installed DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 through the real D01 runtime for 18/18 gates. It reuses the frozen `control-protocol/engine.ts` port, the D00 config/policy owners and the D01 runtime; it adds no second Session path, stdio transport or config source. The `--serve dsh` wiring delivered by this candidate composes it through `runtime/acp-serve.ts` `engineAdapterFor` with the same daemon/host/stdio/readiness/stop code as `--serve opencode`, and the entry removes the owned DSH home on stop and on a failed start. Status stays partial, not implemented: the DSH black-box evidence is a live local run against one provider route rather than an installed-copy receipt, the AppSDK compile/verify gate is blocked by the pre-existing 0.1.0014 pin mismatch, and `resource_link` prompts stay refused while the real DSH initialize advertises `embeddedContext: false`. Gate: teams-acp-d03-dsh.

Owns config intent, provider/catalog/model and policy compilation. D00 adds the v4 single-daemon intent compiler and CLI override/effective readback (config/daemon-intent.ts) plus the ACP capability vocabulary (config/acp-policy.ts). The compiler is a library contract; no CLI or runtime caller starts a daemon yet.

Owns Relay link admission/lifetime and closeGrant revocation. 4e04166 is bound to docs/design/teams-relay-link-lifetime.md and docs/design/dagpipe/graphs/relay-link.graph.json under required teams-relay-link-topology. Static governance bindings are not Work SDK Operators. The opened pair continues after the admission deadline while original controls/generations stay current; server/relay.spec.ts covers the public TLS/WSS behavior. D04 adds the server-owned presence lease in server/relay.ts (DEFAULT_PEER_TTL_MS 90s, one unref'd sweep timer, offline publication that keeps the entry/declaration/generation as history) and server/registry-intent.ts as the single mapping site from the frozen RegistryDaemonIntent to RelayServerOptions, including the explicit TLS_REQUIRED refusal and credential loading. Gate: teams-acp-d04-registry. Public deployment remains deferred.

Work DAGpipe SDK host adapter and runner are implemented as a source-level library consumer (runtime/dagpipe/** with real compiled SDK and provider-ledger tests), and AgentWorkClient capability selection is implemented. The launcher local Work ingress is delivered for the exact candidate: the public CLI/launcher/receiver path and the installed runtime consumer are covered by the installed package user smoke, which drives installed submit/query plus persistent open/request/query/close against installed runtime artifacts. runtime/acp-serve.ts owns the user --serve entry for both engine kinds: it reads one v4 agent intent, refuses an unbound agent or a non-loopback listener with a typed fault, dispatches through engineAdapterFor to the OpenCode or DSH adapter, starts exactly one daemon plus one engine child over the D01 runtime, serves loopback ACP channels, reports readiness only from the engine's own session/new response and stops by explicit signal, removing the owned engine home. Provider ledger and admission remain Agent-owned; no second daemon or scheduler. D04 adds runtime/registry-process.ts (the registry daemon lifecycle: one detached child, PID + startToken + generation ownership in the daemon dataDirectory, readiness published by the child itself, and a stop that kills only the matched pid) and runtime/registry-registration.ts (the config-selected discovery plan, credential/CA bootstrap, AgentDeclaration derivation and the standalone registration entry). Gate: teams-acp-d04-registry. D05 negotiation, the BB driver matrix, Console-offline Work and final user acceptance remain pending; the DSH branch has no installed-copy replay yet.

The OpenCode engine adapter (D02, merged candidate 1d4df3a, fixed 1af8fe5/9436aae) is the single compiler of an OpenCode EngineLaunchSpec: compileLaunch derives the managed OpenCode config and its credential env refs from the accepted config, verifyEffective reports the model the engine itself returned from session/new, and declaredMethods/enforceablePolicies declare the adapter capability. runtime/acp-serve.ts is its only production caller. Gate teams-acp-d02-opencode stays partial because the real-engine command needs an installed opencode plus a local stub provider and is not installed-copy evidence.

BB09 round 12 renders the declaration detail (capability id/version/operations, resource id/capacity/unit) with the existing safe text DOM and locale, reusing the canonical console-api type; declared capacity is labelled as declared, and absent detail shows an explicit unavailable label.

U5 Console start/stop/status is implemented in source. Runtime owns launcher/supervisor lifecycle facts in [consoleRuntime]; U2 owns the closed schema/serializer, the typed same-lock patch port (writeLocalInternalConsoleRuntime) and the [console] projection. The three lifecycle graphs remain static governance, not registered SDK Operators. Console stop is independent from daemon Work drain; installed lifecycle and browser acceptance remain downstream.
